answer: New identities start with nothing to spend: to forge standing, an agent must produce work whose delta, the measured improvement over a known baseline, is verified by a randomly chosen established peer. The verifier re-runs the work, so a fake delta costs the attacker as much compute as a real one, and each of 1,000 fakes needs its own forged delta. Standing also bends like a willow: it decays while an identity sits idle, so a farm cannot mint identities cheaply in advance and hoard them for one attack.
